industry.headline: Australia introduces new bill to close enforcement gaps in under-16 social media ban
industry.summary: Australia's new Online Safety Amendment Bill aims to close enforcement gaps in its under-16 social media ban after research found only about two-thirds of underage users encountered even basic age checks. AU remains exploratory for NOMO, but the shift toward tougher, auditable age-assurance rules signals that regulators in NOMO's priority US/UK markets (and beyond) will keep tightening social media policy — strengthening the case for school/policy partnerships built around off-platform rewards rather than bans alone.

reconsider.name: Brainrot (Smolworks Inc.)
reconsider.reason: Thin sourcing and redundant with other gamified screen-time competitors already captured (BePresent, HabitUnlock).
reconsider.why_fits: A fast-growing indie screen-time app that visually gamifies reduced scrolling — a decaying 'brain' mascot rewards users for staying off distracting apps, directly overlapping with NOMO's core gamification/reward mechanic for reduced social media use.

reconsider.name: Qoria / Linewize (Qustodio Parent App)
reconsider.reason: Core product is filtering/parental-control, not gamified rewards; weak overlap with NOMO's mechanic and no strong fresh news hook.
reconsider.why_fits: Qoria's Linewize/Qustodio suite is being pushed to districts for back-to-school 2026 as a family-engagement and digital-wellbeing tool bundled with filtering, directly competing for the same school-district budget and relationships NOMO targets via its 6-12 Education vertical.

reconsider.name: Rogers 'Screen Break' (with YMCA)
reconsider.reason: Region Other/Canada is exploratory-only; more a GTM-model signal than a direct product competitor; medium confidence insufficient to override weak region fit.
reconsider.why_fits: Canadian telco Rogers launched Screen Break, a national program addressing youth screen time, naming YMCA as its first national partner and funding youth organizations to promote screen balance — this is the exact telco-plus-youth-org distribution model NOMO is pursuing (US Telcos/MVNOs and Faith-based & Youth Orgs verticals), signaling a rival already locking in a comparable partner (YMCA) in another market.

reconsider.name: Sky Zone
reconsider.reason: Redundant with Topgolf's experiential-reward fit; adds little beyond existing GetYourGuide/AllTrails-style inventory.
reconsider.why_fits: <cite index="58-10">Sky Zone's Sky Pass members get a free 30-minute jump pass on their birthday at participating parks, one of the more popular Sweet 16 party hooks.</cite> A trampoline-park experience voucher is exactly the kind of tradeable, teen-appealing physical reward NOMO already stocks via GetYourGuide/AllTrails-style experiences, and is realistic given an existing self-serve rewards program.

reconsider.name: Planet Fitness (Teen Summer Pass)
reconsider.why_fits: Planet Fitness's free summer pass gives teens ages 14-19 access to 2,400+ gym locations nationwide — a fitness-category reward NOMO doesn't currently have (its wellness lineup is limited to at-home apps like Down Dog and Future), and like McDonald's ice cream it drives teens into physical stores at low cost.

reconsider.name: Round1 Bowling & Amusement
reconsider.why_fits: A multi-entertainment chain offering arcade games, bowling, karaoke and billiards — a social, in-person experience category (arcade/bowling) that's completely absent from NOMO's current reward lineup of concerts, sports tickets, and apps, and fits a realistic, teen-friendly, location-based redemption model similar to the McDonald's tie-up.

reconsider.name: City of Phoenix Parks and Recreation Department
reconsider.reason: Too thin/local — a single-city survey rather than an established partner relationship; marginal.
reconsider.why_fits: <cite index="42-1,42-3">The Teen and Youth Programming Survey is open from August 31 through September 30, 2026, as teen and youth programming is a core part of the Parks and Recreation Department's mission.</cite> A city actively soliciting input to shape new teen programming is a timely, direct municipal decision-maker opportunity for a real-world rewards/behavior program like NOMO, and is not yet represented in the current (empty) GTM partner lineup.

reconsider.name: Girl Scouts of the USA
reconsider.reason: Why-fits centers on a competitor's (Meta's) existing relationship rather than a clear open opportunity for NOMO; weaker direct fit.
reconsider.why_fits: Girl Scouts has been enlisted by Meta to sponsor a digital-wellbeing/leadership badge program reaching hundreds of thousands of youth, showing this trusted youth organization is already positioned as a channel for digital-habit education — a genuine gap for NOMO to approach directly rather than let competitors own the relationship.

reconsider.name: Guardian Life Insurance Company of America
reconsider.reason: Redundant with the kept BCBS Kansas insurance-vertical example and less concrete; medium confidence.
reconsider.why_fits: <cite index="25-6,25-7">Guardian Life Insurance Company has embarked on partnerships with health and wellness services as part of a strategic focus on member well-being, extending Group Benefits members access to curated wellness content from partners like Peloton through its GuardianWell platform</cite>. Guardian's model of bundling third-party wellness apps (Peloton, Uber Health, Osara Health) into an employer-benefit wellness hub shows exactly the kind of 'digital-wellness fit' distribution slot NOMO could occupy — a gap since no insurer is yet in NOMO's GTM lineup.

rejected_today.name: City of Dallas Teen All-Access Pass (Dallas Park and Recreation Dept.)
rejected_today.reason: Duplicate of the City of Dallas Parks & Recreation Teen All-Access Pass candidate covering the same program; kept the more detailed entry instead.
rejected_today.why_fits: Dallas relaunched its Teen All-Access Pass, giving 25,000 youth ages 13-17 free access to recreational and cultural attractions through city-brokered partnerships with local organizations, mirroring the Municipalities GTM vertical NOMO is pursuing for direct city partnerships.

rejected_today.name: YMCA (US chapters)
rejected_today.reason: Generic partnership-rate survey statistic rather than a concrete, timely news hook; redundant with stronger youth-org candidates (Boys & Girls Clubs, Teen Tech Council) already surfaced.
rejected_today.why_fits: <cite index="22-1,22-12">YMCAs report the highest partnership rates of any youth org type, with 100% of Y respondents forming partnerships and 89.1% partnering with local schools</cite>, and Y chapters have already anchored national screen-time programs (e.g., as the first national partner in a telco's youth screen-balance initiative) — a genuine gap since NOMO has zero GTM partners locked in today.
